title: Machine Learning-Based Classification of Soccer Attacking Phases Using Spatiotemporal Tracking Features
author: Jack Chiang
abstract: This study investigates whether player and ball tracking data can be used to automatically classify attacking phases in soccer. Using SkillCorner Open Data from 10 Australian A-League matches, we processed tracking information into 2,955 attacking phases, each represented by 18 numerical features describing ball movement, team shape, player spacing, defensive pressure, and temporal characteristics. We evaluated multiple supervised machine learning algorithms to classify five attacking phases: build-up, creation, direct attack, fast transition, and finishing. Enhanced XGBoost achieved the highest test accuracy of 91.9%, with a macro F1 score of 0.864, while Enhanced Random Forest achieved the highest macro F1 score of 0.873. Ball starting position, forward progress, and phase duration-related measurements were particularly informative. Fast transitions were the most difficult to classify, likely due to class imbalance and similarities with other attacking phases. These findings demonstrate the potential of interpretable, feature-based machine learning methods to support soccer tactical analysis, although additional evaluation across leagues and matches is necessary to assess generalizability.
